answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an farming party who spins up 249 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 109 times the capital for one share. The plume report publishes the merge explicitly at each sable. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
